_comment: The gnome's notes. 'daily' is indexed by days sober (0 = the sober date, up to 30). 'months' is 1 to 11 months. 'years' is: 1 year, 2-4, 5, 6-9, 10 and up ({n} becomes the number). 'rainy' rotates on wet or foggy days after the first month; index 2 is used for storms and 4 for fog. 'activity' is one line per pose, in pose order, shown on his page on ordinary days.

daily.full: The hardest step is the first one. You took it. I'm glad you're here.
One full day behind you. That first one is the biggest of all.
Yesterday you did it once. Today you get to do it again.
Day three can feel rough. Rest, eat something good, and go easy on yourself.
You kept showing up. That's the whole trick, really.
I watered the seed this morning. You've been tending something too.
Six days. Tomorrow makes a week, but today is the one that counts.
A full week. Seven mornings you chose this. I'm proud of you.
Week two starts here. Same plan as before: just today.
Slow and steady grows the strongest roots.
Ten days. Look how far the little sprout has come already.
When today feels like a lot, shrink it. The next hour is enough.
Cravings pass, like weather. You've outlasted every one so far.
Someone would love to hear from you today. Maybe give them a call.
Fourteen days. The sprout is standing up, and so are you.
Fifteen days. You don't have to do the next fifteen today. Only this one.
It's an old saying because it works. Today is all there is to do.
Talk to yourself the way you'd talk to a friend who was trying this hard.
Roots grow where nobody can see them. A lot is happening in you.
You're building something real, one ordinary day after another.
Twenty. I had to count on my fingers and my boots.
Three weeks of mornings. This is starting to look like a habit.
Tired is allowed. Resting is part of growing, not a break from it.
Asking isn't weakness. Even I need a hand with the heavy watering can.
No need to rush anything today. Easy does it.
Twenty-five days ago this felt impossible. Here you are.
Name one small good thing from today. I'll go first: you're here.
Three days from a month. Keep your eyes on today all the same.
Four full weeks. The first leaf is nearly ready to open.
Tomorrow is a big one. Tonight, just rest.
Thirty days. Look back at day one for a second. Then carry on, same as ever.

months.full: One whole month, and the first leaf is out. Wonderful work.
Sixty days or so, and a second leaf. You're growing, plain as day.
A quarter of a year. A new branch today. That takes real strength.
Four months of showing up. The little tree is looking sure of itself.
Five leaves for five months. I polished each one this morning.
Six months. Half a year of days, each one chosen. I'm so proud of you.
Seven months. Lucky number, though luck had nothing to do with it.
Eight months in. Your roots go deeper than you think.
Nine months. A new branch, and so much new in you too.
Ten months. I've run out of fingers again. Keep going.
Eleven months. The big one is close. Today still comes first.

years.full: A whole year. The tree gave its first apple today, and it's yours. Happy birthday.
Two years, and a second apple on the branch. Look what your days added up to.
Three years. Three apples now, and the tree is getting tall. So are you.
Four years. Four apples, and I've been saving planks. You'll see why next year.
Five years. The tree is fully grown, so I built a little house in it. Come visit.
Six years. I made the house wider and put in a new window. More light now.
Seven years. A second floor went up, and a cat moved in. She picked us, I think.
Eight years. Someone special moved in, and brought a dog. The house is full now.
Nine years. A new attic window. On clear nights we can see the stars up there.
Ten years. The house is finished, deck and all, and a robin took the attic. Home.
Eleven years. A stream came down the hill, so I built a bridge. Let's explore.
Twelve years. Nothing new to build today. Just a quiet morning on the deck with you.
Thirteen years. We dug a well. Fresh water for anyone who wanders by thirsty.
Fourteen years. The path over the bridge is worn smooth. That's a lot of good days.
Fifteen years. An old friend built a cottage on the far hill. Neighbours at last!
{n} years. Look at the little world your days have built. I love living in it.

rainy.full: Trees need rainy days too. This one is doing its work.
Grey day. I'll sit here with you until it passes.
I've never met a storm that stayed. This one won't either.
Kettle's on. Nothing to fix today, only to get through.
Can't see far in the fog. You only need to see today anyway.
Wet days are good days to ring someone who gets it.

activity: Just keeping an eye on things today.
Good to see you. I was hoping you'd stop by.
A little water, a little patience. That's all it takes.
Tidying up under the tree. It likes a neat lawn.
A quiet day with a good book.
Tea time. Pull up a patch of grass.
Resting my eyes. Only for a minute.
A bit of light for a grey day.
Rain is good for the tree. I brought the umbrella.
What a day! I'm so proud of you.
